cues.text: The first problem begins when a team measures activity instead of learning.
A full queue can look productive while every important assumption remains untested.
The useful shift is to rank work by how much uncertainty it removes.
That gives the team a concrete reason to run the smallest decisive experiment first.

A second trap appears when teams treat a roadmap as a promise rather than a hypothesis.
The plan then hides uncertainty behind dates and polished project names.
A roadmap is stronger when each item states what evidence would change the decision.
Now leaders can revise direction without pretending that learning is failure.
The future belongs to people who can change their minds faster than everyone else.
In other words, rapid belief revision is the durable advantage.
The final pattern concerns retrospectives that catalog events but never alter behavior.
Teams often leave with a detailed timeline and no owner for the next experiment.
A retrospective creates value only when one observation becomes a testable operating change.

clips.title: Prioritize work by uncertainty removed
clips.contextSummary: Busy queues can conceal that important assumptions remain untested.
clips.insightSummary: Rank work by the amount of uncertainty it can remove.
clips.payoffSummary: Run the smallest decisive experiment before committing more effort.

clips.title: Turn roadmap promises into testable hypotheses
clips.contextSummary: Dates and polished project names can hide uncertainty in a roadmap.
clips.insightSummary: Each roadmap item should name the evidence that would change the decision.
clips.payoffSummary: Leaders can revise direction without treating new learning as failure.

clips.title: Make retrospectives produce operating experiments
clips.contextSummary: Retrospectives often create timelines without assigning the next experiment.
clips.insightSummary: An observation creates value when it becomes a testable operating change.
clips.payoffSummary: Predict the result, then keep or revert the change using observed evidence.
